objective: Every order is taken, picked and delivered with its status always known

open.text: ANSWERED (2026-10-04, the warehouse team's runbook, section 4.2): orders placed after the cut-off are held until the next picking wave, which starts at 06:00 local time on working days; a held order keeps its place in the queue and is never re-priced. The runbook also says a held order can be released early by a supervisor from the picking screen, which writes a release record with the supervisor's id and the reason, and that released orders join the current wave at its end rather than its start. Weekend orders wait for Monday unless the site runs a Saturday wave, which is set per site in the configuration and is off by default.
ANSWERED (2026-10-03, ops): refunds go through the payment provider's API, never through the order store directly.
Does a cancelled order keep its id, or is the id freed for reuse?
PARTLY ANSWERED (2026-10-02): stock is reserved at checkout; still open: how long a reservation lasts when payment stalls.
ANSWERED (2026-10-01, the API owner): order ids are UUIDv7, generated by the service, never by the client.
Who may change an order after it is picked: the customer, support, or nobody?
ANSWERED (2026-10-04): an order's address is frozen at payment; later changes are a new delivery, not an edit.
Is there a limit on items per order, and if so is it enforced by the API or by the store?
Do we keep a full history of status changes, or only the current status and its time?
